CONTRACT (orchestrator-authored; treat as the ticket body)

Deliverable: lib/specled_ex/config.ex ~line 120 — update the moduledoc sentence "the 12 guardrail codes (10 append_only/* + 2 overlap/*)" to the true figures: 13 guardrail codes (11 append_only/* + 2 overlap/*). Verify the counts yourself against the emitters in lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex and lib/specled_ex/overlap.ex before writing them. Scan the REST of config.ex whole-file for any other count/code-list claim about these namespaces and fix any that are false the same way (report each in the completion record); touch nothing else.

Spec co-change is AUTHORIZED where the gate forces it: the smallest edit to .spec/specs/config.spec.md (or any other subject the branch guard names) that keeps branch_guard_missing_subject_update green; .spec/realization_hashes.json refresh only if a named binding drifts (a moduledoc-only change should not). A Spec-Drift trailer for branch_guard_missing_decision_update with a one-line reason is the expected remedy if that finding fires — .spec/decisions/** is out of scope.

Out of Scope (files): everything else, including VERSION, CHANGELOG.md, docs/**, .spec/decisions/**, all other lib/ and test/ files

Session: 63655cb6-965a-48c3-bb59-64da6ce31142
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-specled-ex/63655cb6-965a-48c3-bb59-64da6ce31142.jsonl

Mechanical checks:
- Files touched: 2 — lib/specled_ex/config.ex, .spec/specs/config.spec.md (git diff --name-status b255dbd5..HEAD). .spec/realization_hashes.json NOT touched, as the contract predicted for a moduledoc-only change.
- Files outside Allowed globs: 0
- config.ex change is prose-only: PROVEN. `git diff -U0` shows exactly one changed line in the whole file, line 120. The enclosing `@moduledoc """` heredoc spans lines 108-127, so line 120 is strictly interior. No AST-affecting text changed; no `execute:` flips anywhere in the diff.
- Gate-forced spec touch: NOT PROVEN — counterfactual contradicts it. Real detached-HEAD commit 964de8cc (tree of 9f8ab1e8 with .spec/specs/config.spec.md restored to b255dbd5) run against `mix spec.check --no-run-commands --base b255dbd5` returned `spec.check result=pass`, exit 0, findings=1 (error=0 warning=0 info=1). The single finding IS `branch_guard_missing_subject_update` on lib/specled_ex/config.ex, but at INFO severity, self-described: "realization attested binding(s) ... as clean — informational only." The gate stays green without the spec edit. Per the stated criterion (counterfactual "must fail"), the co-change is not forced. Detached commit discarded; branch restored to 9f8ab1e8.
- Spec-Drift trailer: none present, and none needed — `mix spec.check --no-run-commands --base b255dbd5` on the real HEAD passes with findings=0.

Semantic checks:
- Counts derived independently: append_only = 11, overlap = 2, total 13. Method: unique `"append_only/<code>"` literals in lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex (builders at lines 377-558) and `"overlap/<code>"` in lib/specled_ex/overlap.ex (lines 109, 125). Cross-checked against the default severity catalog in lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex:26-39, which enumerates the identical 11 + 2. Repo-wide sweep of lib/ finds no additional codes in either namespace (the only other hits are branch_check.ex's catalog and a `String.starts_with?(code, "append_only/")` prefix test in review/html.ex:3508). Claim in diff: "the 13 guardrail codes (11 `append_only/*` + 2 `overlap/*`)" — MATCH on all three numerals.
- Whole-file config.ex scan: the numeral sweep over the whole file surfaces no other count, code-list, or identifier claim about these namespaces. Lines 115-116 show `append_only/requirement_deleted` and `overlap/duplicate_covers` as YAML examples — both are real codes, so no falsehood. The implementer's "none" is confirmed for counts. It is NOT confirmed for the provenance clause in the same sentence — see Gap 1.
- Provenance wording: FALSE AS WRITTEN — this is the blocking finding. See Gap 1.
- Targeted verification: all pass on real HEAD. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` (clean), `mix format --check-formatted` (exit 0), `mix test test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs` (19 tests, 0 failures), `mix spec.check --no-run-commands --base b255dbd5` (validate status=pass, findings=0, `spec.check result=pass`).
- Requirements coverage: no behavior change and no new tests are expected here, and none appear — correct for a prose-only sweep. The touched surface is the `SpecLedEx.Config.Guardrails` moduledoc only; the specled.config musts covering config parse and defaults are untouched and their verifications pass under the structural gate above.
- Working tree restored: clean except `?? .grok/sandbox.toml`, an untracked harness artifact timestamped 10:25 (before the 10:30 implementation commit). Not in the commit, not created by this verification.

Verdict: FAIL

Gaps:

Gap 1 (blocking) — false provenance claim introduced by this edit.
  Where: lib/specled_ex/config.ex:120-121 (hexdocs-rendered).
  Reads: "The code key namespace is the 13 guardrail codes (11 `append_only/*` + 2 `overlap/*`) introduced by specled_-fm4."
  Why false: `git log -S` per code proves 12 of the 13 came from specled_-fm4 (commit 556085fe / fm4.3 introduced exactly 10 append_only codes; 2b6cba28 / fm4.4 introduced both overlap codes). The 11th append_only code, `append_only/self_authorized_weakening`, was introduced by commit 20046ffe on this very branch, ticket specled_-q0q.2. Both readings of the clause are false: as an appositive it attributes all 13 to fm4; as a restrictive modifier it says the namespace is only fm4's codes, which contradicts the "13" it modifies.
  Note the regression direction: before this edit the sentence was provenance-ACCURATE ("the 12 guardrail codes (10 + 2) introduced by specled_-fm4" — exactly fm4's set). Bumping the numerals while leaving the attribution in place converted a true clause into a false one. The stale count was fixed; a new falsehood was created in the same sentence.
  Remedy (either is acceptable): drop "introduced by specled_-fm4" entirely — a dropped provenance claim is in scope and fine; or widen it truthfully, e.g. "introduced by specled_-fm4 and extended by specled_-q0q.2". Prose-only, same Allowed glob, no behavior change.

Gap 2 (minor, scope) — .spec/specs/config.spec.md touched without the gate forcing it.
  The contract authorizes spec co-change "where the gate forces it". The counterfactual above shows the gate does not: without the edit, spec.check still passes, downgrading branch_guard_missing_subject_update to informational because the realization attestation reports the config bindings clean.
  Mitigating: the edit is genuinely minimal and harmless — it extends one sentence of an existing "Branch reconciliation note" paragraph and rewraps a second. No spec-requirements or spec-scenarios block is touched, no must is weakened, no verification stub is flipped, and the added prose ("corrects the `Guardrails` moduledoc count to 13 (11 `append_only/*` + 2 `overlap/*`)") is itself factually correct.
  Recording this as a Gap because the authorization was conditional and the condition is not met; the orchestrator may reasonably waive it. Flagging rather than deciding: "keeps branch_guard_missing_subject_update green" is ambiguous between "zero findings" (the edit does achieve this) and "gate passes" (true either way).

Notes (advisory only):
- The numeric half of the deliverable is correct and independently confirmed. Gap 1 is a one-clause prose fix in the line already being edited; it does not require re-opening any other file.
- The 13-code figure now agrees with three independent surfaces: the emitters, branch_check.ex's default catalog, and the config.spec.md branch note. Worth keeping that agreement in mind as the invariant to re-check if a 14th code lands.
- `.grok/sandbox.toml` is untracked in the stage worktree and counted by the branch guard's changed-files tally on a dirty tree (changed_files=3 vs the commit's 2). Harmless here since findings=0, but someone should sweep it before the release cut.

AUDIT: BOUNCE → implementer
Session: 63655cb6-965a-48c3-bb59-64da6ce31142
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-specled-ex/63655cb6-965a-48c3-bb59-64da6ce31142.jsonl

Reasoning: Gap 1 CONFIRMED independently. `git show 556085fe:lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex | grep -o '"append_only/[a-z_]*"' | sort -u | wc -l` returns exactly 10, and 2b6cba28 (fm4.4) introduced both `overlap/*` codes — so specled_-fm4 contributed 12 codes, not 13. `git log -S "append_only/self_authorized_weakening" --oneline -- lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex` returns a single commit, 20046ffe (specled_-q0q.2), for the eleventh code. The sentence now at lib/specled_ex/config.ex:120-121 therefore attributes 13 codes to a ticket that introduced 12, and the pre-edit text ("12 ... introduced by specled_-fm4") was true — this edit converted a true clause into a false one, which is exactly the failure class this scope-expansion chain exists to eliminate. Gap 2 RULING: WAIVED, binding. The contract's condition reads "the smallest edit ... that keeps branch_guard_missing_subject_update green," and eliminating the finding is a defensible reading of "keeps green" even though the counterfactual shows the gate also passes without it; the edit is confined to an existing Branch-reconciliation-note paragraph (.spec/specs/config.spec.md:168-173), touches no spec-requirements, spec-scenarios, or verification block, weakens no must, and its added prose is factually correct. Forcing removal buys zero substance. Not a precedent for unforced spec edits: it is a waiver on an ambiguous contract clause, and future contracts should say "counterfactual must fail" if that is the intent. Hygiene otherwise clean — `git diff --name-status b255dbd5..9f8ab1e8` shows exactly the 2 Allowed files, .spec/realization_hashes.json untouched, config.ex changed on one line strictly interior to the `@moduledoc """` heredoc spanning 108-127 (verified by reading 105-130), zero behavior change. The 11 + 2 = 13 count itself is correct against the emitters. A whole-file sweep of config.ex confirms line 121 is the only `specled_-` provenance claim and line 120 the only count claim in the file, so this is the last one.

Bounce reason: One prose fix in lib/specled_ex/config.ex, in the line pair you already edited. Line 120-121 currently reads:

    namespace is the 13 guardrail codes (11 `append_only/*` + 2 `overlap/*`)
    introduced by specled_-fm4. `branch_guard.severities` covers its own

The clause "introduced by specled_-fm4" is now false: fm4 introduced 12 of the 13 (10 append_only via 556085fe, 2 overlap via 2b6cba28); the eleventh append_only code, `append_only/self_authorized_weakening`, came from 20046ffe on this branch under specled_-q0q.2. Fix it either way:

- Preferred — widen it truthfully: "... + 2 `overlap/*`) introduced by specled_-fm4 and extended by specled_-q0q.2."
- Acceptable — drop the attribution entirely, ending the sentence at the closing paren.

Keep the moduledoc heredoc's existing wrap width and leave the rest of the sentence ("`branch_guard.severities` covers its own namespace; ...") intact. Do not touch .spec/specs/config.spec.md again — that edit is waived as-is and is factually correct; re-opening it would be new unforced scope. .spec/realization_hashes.json should still not need a refresh (moduledoc-only). Amend or add a commit on the same branch, re-run the final tier per the contract, and post a fresh IMPLEMENTED record noting the provenance correction.

Housekeeping (not blocking, not for this ticket): `.grok/sandbox.toml` is untracked in the stage worktree and inflates the branch guard's changed-files tally on a dirty tree. Someone should sweep it before the 0.13.0 cut.

Mechanical checks:
- Cumulative files (git diff b255dbd5..HEAD --name-status): exactly 2 — M .spec/specs/config.spec.md, M lib/specled_ex/config.ex. Nothing outside the Allowed globs; .spec/realization_hashes.json untouched across the whole range, as predicted for a moduledoc-only change.
- Round-2 increment (git show 87531f84 --name-status): 1 file — M lib/specled_ex/config.ex. Stat: 2 insertions, 1 deletion. Zero .spec/ paths in the commit.
- Prose-only: PROVEN MECHANICALLY, not merely by inspection. Parsed 9f8ab1e8:lib/specled_ex/config.ex and 87531f84:lib/specled_ex/config.ex with Code.string_to_quoted!/1 and compared Macro.to_string/1 of each. Raw ASTs differ (expected — the doc string text changed); after prewalking both and replacing every @moduledoc/@doc string literal with a sentinel atom, the two ASTs are IDENTICAL. So the sole delta in the file is the content of a documentation string literal; no expression, clause, attribute, guard, or arity changed. Positionally consistent: the @moduledoc """ heredoc opens at config.ex:108 and closes at :128, and the changed lines are 121-122, strictly interior. No execute: flips anywhere in the range.
- config.spec.md untouched in round 2: YES. The waived round-1 edit is carried forward unmodified from 9f8ab1e8; 87531f84 does not re-open it. Not re-flagged, per the binding waiver.
- .grok handling did not leak: confirmed. `git diff b255dbd5..HEAD --name-only | grep -i grok` returns nothing, so no .grok path is in either commit. .grok/sandbox.toml is now absent from disk entirely and `git status --porcelain -uall` is EMPTY — the round-1 untracked residue was swept, so the branch guard's changed-files tally is now 2 on a clean tree (it read 3 on the dirty tree in round 1). The .grok/hooks/* and .grok/rules/* files that are tracked at HEAD are pre-existing repo infrastructure, present at b255dbd5 and unmodified by this ticket.

Semantic checks:
- Corrected sentence text, verbatim from config.ex:119-124 (heredoc body, hexdocs-rendered):

      Each entry is `code => severity` where severity is one of `off`, `info`,
      `warning`, `error` (see `SpecLedEx.BranchCheck.Severity`). The code key
      namespace is the 13 guardrail codes (11 `append_only/*` + 2 `overlap/*`)
      introduced by specled_-fm4 and extended by specled_-q0q.2.
      `branch_guard.severities` covers its own
      namespace; the two maps are kept separate (not merged) so the two
      guardrail surfaces stay legible in config.

  The audit's preferred remedy was adopted verbatim ("introduced by specled_-fm4 and extended by specled_-q0q.2"), and the rest of the sentence is intact.

- Every claim in the sentence verified independently (whole-sentence re-check per the epic lesson):

  CLAIM "11 `append_only/*`" — TRUE. `grep -o '"append_only/[a-z_]*"' lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex | sort -u` yields exactly 11 distinct codes: adr_affects_widened, decision_deleted, disabled_without_reason, missing_change_type, must_downgraded, negative_removed, no_baseline, requirement_deleted, same_pr_self_authorization, scenario_regression, self_authorized_weakening.

  CLAIM "2 `overlap/*`" — TRUE. Same method over lib/specled_ex/overlap.ex yields duplicate_covers and must_stem_collision.

  CLAIM "the 13 guardrail codes" — TRUE, and exhaustive, not just arithmetically consistent. A repo-wide sweep `grep -rhoE '"(append_only|overlap)/[a-z_]+"' lib/ | sort -u` returns exactly 13 unique tokens across only three files (append_only.ex, overlap.ex, branch_check.ex — the last being the default severity catalog, which enumerates the identical set). There is no fourteenth code emitted anywhere in lib/, so the definite description "the 13 guardrail codes" is not an overclaim.

  CLAIM "introduced by specled_-fm4" — TRUE for 12 of the 13, which is what the widened clause now asserts. Per-code `git log -S '"<code>"' --oneline --reverse` on the owning emitter file: all 10 append_only codes trace to 556085fe ("specled_-fm4.3: AppendOnly module + fixture builder + normalize_for_state (W2a)"), and both overlap codes trace to 2b6cba28 ("specled_-fm4.4: Overlap module + AppendOnly/Overlap wiring into BranchCheck (W2b)"). Independently corroborated at the tree level: `git show 556085fe:lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex | grep -o '"append_only/[a-z_]*"' | sort -u | wc -l` = 10.

  CLAIM "and extended by specled_-q0q.2" — TRUE. `git log -S "append_only/self_authorized_weakening" --oneline -- lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex` returns exactly one commit, 20046ffe "feat(append_only): expose same-PR weakening authorization (specled_-q0q.2)" — a commit on this branch belonging to specled_-q0q.2, as the task specified. Ran the -S archaeology on all 13 codes individually rather than only the eleventh, which closes the residual risk the round-1 gap depended on: the provenance clause is now not merely non-false but COMPLETE — every one of the 13 codes is attributed to fm4 or q0q.2, with no third contributor left unnamed. The round-1 falsehood (13 codes attributed wholly to a ticket that introduced 12) is eliminated in both readings, appositive and restrictive.

  CLAIM (trailing clause) "`branch_guard.severities` covers its own namespace" — TRUE. The branch_guard severities map governs a disjoint code set: `grep -rhoE '"branch_guard[_/][a-z_]+"' lib/` returns ten branch_guard_* codes (unmapped_change, missing_subject_update, missing_decision_update, requirement_without_test_tag, realization_drift, dangling_binding, realization_unknown_tier, underspecified_realization, untested_realization, untethered_test) plus, per SpecLedEx.Config.BranchGuard's own moduledoc, bare codes like spec_requirement_too_short. No append_only/* or overlap/* code appears in that surface, and no branch_guard code appears in the guardrails surface.

  CLAIM (trailing clause) "the two maps are kept separate (not merged)" — TRUE, verified in code rather than by wording. config.ex build/1 reads "branch_guard" and "guardrails" into separate maps (lines 271-272), parses each through its own module (BranchGuard.parse/1, Guardrails.parse/1 at 277-278), and stores them as two distinct struct fields (293-294). branch_check.ex:183-184 then threads them through as two separate options, config_severities: config.branch_guard.severities and guardrails_severities: config.guardrails.severities. No merge anywhere on that path.

- Unchanged-but-adjacent claims re-checked (they share the moduledoc and would be my responsibility if false): the YAML examples at config.ex:115-116 name append_only/requirement_deleted and overlap/duplicate_covers, both real emitted codes; the closing line's "mirroring `SpecLedEx.Config.BranchGuard` exactly" matches that module's own moduledoc, which states the same reject-and-drop-with-diagnostic behavior. No other count, code-list, or specled_- provenance claim exists elsewhere in config.ex.

- Targeted verification (all on real HEAD 87531f84, clean tree): PASS.
  - `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` — exit 0, no output.
  - `mix format --check-formatted` — exit 0.
  - `mix spec.check --no-run-commands --base b255dbd5` — exit 0. `validate status=pass errors=0 warnings=0`; subjects=34 requirements=440; `branch base=b255dbd5 changed_files=2 findings=0 (error=0 warning=0 info=0)`; change_type=single_subject; impacted_subjects=specled.config; verdict line `spec.check result=pass`. Note the round-1 informational branch_guard_missing_subject_update is gone now that the tree is clean of the .grok residue — findings is a true zero.
  - `mix test test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs` — 19 tests, 0 failures.
- Working tree state: `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` returns nothing. Fully clean, no untracked residue, branch at 87531f84.
- Full-suite verification: not run by verifier (by design)

Verdict: PASS

Notes (advisory only):
- The one nit, deliberately not a gap: the fix was applied as an inserted line break rather than a reflow, so config.ex:122 ("`branch_guard.severities` covers its own") is a ~44-character line sitting among ~72-character neighbors. It is ragged in the source and invisible in rendered hexdocs, since Markdown reflows the paragraph. The audit asked to keep the existing wrap width, and no existing line was rewrapped, so the instruction was honored on the letter. Nothing is false and the formatter does not touch heredoc bodies. A one-line reflow of 121-124 would tidy it if someone is in the file anyway — not worth a round trip on its own.
- test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs passing is a genuine no-regression signal but is NOT evidence for the provenance claim: that lint guards fabricated finding codes across the docs/skills/.spec corpus and has no notion of ticket identifiers, so "specled_-q0q.2" passes through it unexamined. The git -S archaeology above is the only thing standing behind the provenance sentence — worth knowing if this class of claim recurs, because there is no mechanical gate that would have caught the round-1 falsehood.
- Standing invariant for the release: the 13-code figure now agrees across four independent surfaces — the emitters in append_only.ex/overlap.ex, the default catalog in branch_check.ex:15-39, this moduledoc, and the config.spec.md branch note.
